title: List of Forms and Contact Details Required to Request Medical Records From Northwell Health in 2026
summary: A 2026 guide to Northwell Health medical record request forms, HIM contact details, New York fee limits, and authorization tips for personal injury law firms.
body_markdown:
Requesting medical records from Northwell Health takes more than a quick phone call. Northwell operates[28 hospitals](https://jobs.northwell.edu/about_us/) and more than 1,000 outpatient facilities across New York and Connecticut, and its Health Information Management (HIM) setup is decentralized, so each facility has its own contacts, processing schedule, and submission instructions. For personal injury attorneys handling cases that span several Northwell locations, that means paralegal hours spent tracking separate requests, following up with different HIM departments, and fixing authorizations that come back.[Codes Health](https://www.getcodeshealth.com/) takes that workflow off your plate with AI-powered retrieval that checks authorizations before submission, coordinates requests across facilities, and keeps following up until records arrive.


## **Key Takeaways**


-


Northwell uses two main forms: VD001 authorizes disclosure to a named recipient, while VD087 is a request for access by the patient or a personal representative


-


Former Nuvance facilities in the Hudson Valley and Connecticut have their own records contacts, so confirm the route for attorney requests before you submit


-


Sensitive-record disclosures need the patient's specific consent on the authorization, and missing consent can block release of those categories


-


For requests covered by New York Public Health Law § 18, paper-copy charges cannot exceed[$0.75 per page](https://www.nysenate.gov/legislation/laws/PBH/18) , while Connecticut facilities follow Connecticut rules


-


Processing time varies by facility, request scope, and whether extra authorization or identity information is needed, so confirm the expected completion date with the receiving department


-


Codes Health checks requests for errors to help reduce preventable authorization rejections and reports a general average turnaround of a couple of weeks


## **Understanding Your Rights: How to View My Medical Records Online Free**


### **Northwell Health Patient Portal Access**


Patients have the right to access their own medical records, and Northwell offers several portals for doing it. Use Northwell's portal selector on its[medical records page](https://www.northwell.edu/manage-your-care/medical-records) to identify MyNorthwell, FollowMyHealth, or the regional Blue or Green portal. These portals let patients view test results, visit summaries, and other information already available in the system.


Portal access has limits for legal work, though:


-


Portals only show records from systems connected to that portal


-


Older records from before a portal was in place may not appear


-


Complete billing records and imaging often require separate requests


-


Attorney status alone doesn't give you portal access


Counsel should obtain records through authorized sharing, approved proxy arrangements where available, or formal requests. For personal injury cases, the portal is a good starting point for spotting treatment locations and date ranges, but complete retrieval still runs through formal requests to HIM departments.


### **Troubleshooting Online Access**


When patients can't find their records in a portal, common culprits include:


-


Separate accounts created at different facilities


-


Records stored in legacy systems from before a facility joined Northwell


-


Technical errors that need help from the HIM department


For records not available online, patients and their legal representatives submit formal written requests using the appropriate form.


## **Navigating the Past: How to Find Old Medical Records Online**


### **Retrieving Records from Former Nuvance Facilities**


Tracking down historical records takes some planning. Northwell has grown through acquisitions, and records from facilities that joined the system may sit in different archives or legacy databases. The Hudson Valley and Connecticut facilities that came to Northwell from Nuvance Health have their own records contacts, including:


-

-


Putnam Hospital Center (Carmel Hamlet)


-


Vassar Brothers Medical Center (Poughkeepsie)


-


Danbury Hospital


-

For former Nuvance facilities, confirm the route for attorney requests with medicalrecords@nuvancehealth.org or (203) 739-7218. Northwell also lists fax submission at (203) 749-9000, and the centralized processing address is 100 Reserve Road, Danbury, CT 06810. Don't assume the Datavant patient-request portal accepts every attorney request.


### **Utilizing Health Information Exchanges**


Health Information Exchanges (HIEs) and TEFCA networks give authorized participants another way to look for records across connected healthcare systems, which can help when a client can't recall every treatment location. Network participation, permitted exchange purposes, consent, and available data all limit what comes back, so network searches may still require supplemental provider requests.


Codes Health uses provider-location tools and missing-record detection, along with retrieval channels like custodian integrations, proprietary provider networks, patient portals, fax, email, and phone, to help identify treatment sources and gaps that need follow-up.


## **Streamlined Requests: The Northwell Health Medical Records Request Form**


### **Downloading the Northwell Request Form**


Northwell Health uses two primary forms for medical record requests.


**VD001 (Authorization for Release of Health Information)** : VD001 authorizes disclosure to a named recipient, such as your law firm. You'll find it through Northwell's medical records page. Select the treating facility on Northwell's medical records page and follow its submission instructions, which may include:


-


An online submission option, where the facility offers one


-


Fax to the facility's HIM department


-


Email to the facility's HIM department


-


Mail to the facility's HIM address


**VD087 (Request for Access)** : VD087 is a[request for access](https://www.northwell.edu/sites/northwell.edu/files/2022-03/request-for-access-to-health-information-form-english-2022.pdf) by the patient or personal representative. It can make sense when a client prefers to receive records first and then pass them to counsel. Confirm which form and submission route apply to the requester and facility.


### **Completing the Form Accurately**


Use the current[VD001 authorization](https://www.northwell.edu/sites/northwell.edu/files/2022-03/release-of-health-information-form-english.pdf) supplied for the treating facility. Complete the patient identifiers, releasing provider, recipient, delivery method, requested records, disclosure purpose, expiration, and signature fields. Follow that version's instructions for sensitive-record consent and permission to discuss information verbally. Form versions differ, so check section numbers against the specific form you're using.


Have the patient review and authorize any sensitive-record disclosures needed for the request. Missing required consent may prevent release of those categories or require clarification.

### **Information to Have Ready**


When you call an HIM department, keep this handy:


-

-


Approximate dates of service


-


Type of records needed (medical, billing, imaging)


-


Your authorization submission date and method


-


Fax confirmation number, if applicable


Confirm receipt and follow up according to the department's expected processing schedule.


## **Navigating HIPAA: Your Medical Release Form and Authorization**


### **Filling Out a HIPAA Authorization for Family Members**


When requesting records on a patient's behalf, the authorization should be clear about who receives what and for how long. For attorneys, that means including:


-


**Recipient language** : Identify the law firm as the authorized recipient. If someone signs for the patient, document that person's applicable legal authority.


-


**Scope of authorization** : Specific record types and date ranges to be released


-


**Expiration provisions** : Use an expiration date or event appropriate to the disclosure and consistent with the current form's instructions


-


**Revocation rights** : Acknowledgment that the patient can revoke the authorization in writing


For requests governed by[HIPAA's right of access](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-45/subtitle-A/subchapter-C/part-164/subpart-E/section-164.524) , providers generally must act within 30 calendar days. One extension of up to 30 additional days is permitted with timely written notice explaining the delay and stating the completion date. Other request routes may have different requirements. New York's access law also separates inspection, which must be allowed within ten days, from copies, which must be provided within a reasonable time, so don't treat the inspection period as a copy-delivery deadline.


The New York provisions in this guide apply to relevant New York requests. Connecticut facilities are subject to Connecticut requirements and applicable federal law; verify their fees, deadlines, and representative-documentation requirements separately.


### **Special Considerations for Minors' Records**


Confirm who may authorize disclosure of the specific records. Parent or guardian access has exceptions, particularly for confidential services. Once the patient is an adult, obtain the adult patient's authorization or other applicable authority. Depending on the situation, you may also need:


-


Proof of legal guardianship or parental rights


-


Court orders if custody is shared or disputed


Incomplete authorizations can delay processing, and across medical record retrieval they're a leading preventable cause of denied requests. Missing patient signatures, unclear expiration dates, or unchecked boxes for sensitive records can hold up a request until they're fixed. Correct any identified deficiency and confirm the request's status with the receiving department. Codes Health's AI review is designed to catch these errors before submission, automatically flagging misspellings, missing dates of service, and signature issues that would otherwise lead to provider rejections.


## **Beyond Basic Retrieval: What Are Medical Records and How Are They Used?**


### **Types of Information in Your Medical Records**


Medical records cover far more than physician notes. A complete record set for litigation usually includes:


-


**Clinical records** : History and physical examinations, progress notes, discharge summaries


-


**Diagnostic reports** : Laboratory results, pathology findings, imaging interpretations


-


**Treatment documentation** : Operative reports, procedure notes, therapy records


-


**Nursing records** : Vital signs, medication administration, nursing assessments


-


**Billing records** : Itemized charges, CPT codes, diagnosis codes


-


**Imaging studies** : X-rays, MRIs, CT scans (often requiring separate requests)


For personal injury cases, billing records matter a lot when establishing damages. They provide the cost documentation that supports demand packages and settlement negotiations.


### **Importance of Complete Medical Records**


Incomplete records weaken case value. Commonly missing pieces include:


-


Emergency department records from initial treatment


-


Follow-up specialist consultations


-


Physical therapy and rehabilitation notes


-


Prescription records showing medication history


-


Pre-existing condition documentation that opposing counsel will look for


Codes Health's AI-powered case chronologies organize records chronologically, grouping patient encounters and bills by visit, so large record sets don't have to be sorted by hand. The platform also flags gaps in treatment or documentation, helping legal teams request specific missing records instead of repeating broad requests.

## **Frequently Asked Questions**


### **What is the difference between a medical release form and a HIPAA authorization form?**


A medical release form is a general term for any document that authorizes disclosure of medical information. A HIPAA authorization is a specific type of release that meets federal requirements under[45 CFR § 164.508](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-45/section-164.508) . For Northwell requests, VD001 serves as the authorization for disclosure to a named recipient. It needs core elements such as a description of the information, the recipient, the purpose, an expiration date or event, and the patient's signature. A generic release missing these elements may not be accepted.


### **Can I request medical records for a deceased family member from Northwell Health?**


Yes, if you have the legal authority. For New York requests, establish the requester's legal authority. Section 18 permits access by a qualifying distributee when no personal representative has been appointed and requires the specified death-certificate documentation. Executors and administrators typically provide letters testamentary or letters of administration. Confirm any additional documentation with Northwell, and verify Connecticut requirements separately.


### **Are there any fees associated with requesting medical records from Northwell Health?**


There can be. For requests covered by New York Public Health Law § 18, reasonable paper-copy charges cannot exceed $0.75 per page. The applicable fee rules depend on the request and requester. Electronic-copy fees depend on the applicable access rules and request circumstances, so confirm the charge with the facility. Patient-access fee protections under[HHS fee guidance](https://www.hhs.gov/hipaa/for-professionals/faq/may-a-covered-entity-charge-individuals-a-fee/index.html) don't automatically apply when records go directly to a law firm or other third party. For other formats or services, ask the receiving department for an itemized estimate.


### **What should I do if I find an error in my Northwell Health medical records?**


Patients can request amendments under HIPAA. Submit a written request to the HIM department where the error exists, explaining what's wrong and including supporting documentation. Northwell generally must act on an amendment request within 60 days. One extension of up to 30 days is allowed with written notice explaining the delay and completion date. If denied, patients may submit a statement of disagreement; subsequent disclosures of the affected information must include the required materials or an accurate summary.


### **How long does it typically take to receive medical records after a request?**


Processing time varies by facility, request scope, and whether additional authorization or identity information is needed. For requests under HIPAA's individual right of access, providers generally must act within 30 calendar days, with one possible 30-day extension given timely written notice. Confirm the expected completion date with the receiving department. Codes Health reports a general average turnaround of a couple of weeks and checks requests for errors to help reduce preventable rejections.
